text:
Maya: putting this here 1: UX + API sketch for a Console card that shows per-routelane attribution + quick "what-if" for routing changes. Goal: make cost/latency impact obvious before flips.
Leo: nice. what exactly is a "lane" in the UI? is it an alias for routing policy bucket (fast/cost/burst) or model-variant tag?
Maya: lane = policy bucket. each lane maps to one or more model variants. UI shows lane label, total tokens, cost/1k, p50, current QPS, and a tiny 1h sparkline of allocation.
Carlos: upstream question 1: router currently emits chosen_model and routing_reason. we don't emit lane_name. easiest fix: add optional lane_name string to router event.
Mei: agree but we should discuss backward-compat: ingestion must treat missing lane_name as "unknown" so older events still show up.
Leo: how big is the schema/ingest work? adding one string seems trivial but telemetry team needs a canary.
Carlos: low-lift on router. telemetry changes: schema bump, update parser + aggregator to include lane_name grouping. also add retention note: we should keep lane attribution for 30d for compare windows.
Maya: UI: default view per-route aggregated across models. Expand to per-model breakdown on click. Also let PMs filter out lanes <0.25% of traffic to reduce noise.
Mei: threshold configurable per-tenant? enterprise customers might want lower/higher. we can expose an org-level setting.
Carlos: privacy check: for Private deployments, router already emits tenant_id. lane_name has no PII but if tenants want obfuscation we can hash lane_name with tenant salt in ingestion.
Leo: hashing will break cross-tenant comparisons but that's OK for Private. Public customers get plain labels. add a flag in ingestion to mask lanes for private clusters.
Maya: API contract idea: single compact endpoint: GET /routes/{route_id}/lanes?start=&end=&buckets=12 returns array of lane rows with fields: lane_id, lane_label, tokens, cost_per_1k, p50_ms, qps, sparkline (12 numbers). small payload.
Carlos: prefer lane_id = stable internal id (uuid) + lane_label friendly name. providers: router will emit lane_id on new events.
Mei: sparkline: prefer counts of tokens per bucket instead of percent so product can compute deltas. 12 buckets for last hour (5m each) seems fine.
Leo: perf note: building these aggregates for high-traffic routes could be heavy if we compute on-demand. we need pre-aggregations in the metrics store with lane dimension.
Carlos: agreed. plan: ingestion materializes hourly + rolling 1h 5m buckets keyed by (route_id, lane_id, tenant_id). Console queries the materialized view. fallback: if materialization not present, compute approximate from sampled events.
Maya: simulation UX: small modal where you paste a proposed routing rule (or select an existing policy) and we show predicted change in lane allocations and estimated delta in cost and p50. Not exact but directional.
Mei: to simulate we need to know selection distribution — easiest: sample recent N requests for route and run the router decision logic locally against sample. but router decisions rely on deterministic hashing + feature flags.
Carlos: solution: export sample traces (1 in 1000 or adjustable) including inputs used in routing and seed. simulation service replays samples through router logic. adds complexity but gives reasonable estimates.
Leo: again privacy: sampled traces must be scrubbed of PII. we can strip user text and keep metadata used for routing.
Maya: rollout UI should surface confidence band: e.g., "predicted cost change: +3.2% (+/- 1.1%)" and sample size.
Mei: implement feature flag exp/console-lane-summaries. default off. telemetry team to run ingest canary, then enable for 10% of orgs.
Carlos: infra-bot: deploy scheduled: router/lane_name/1720012600 -> staging, telemetry/1720013600 -> canary, metrics-materialize/1720017200 -> job, console/1720020800 -> behind exp/console-lane-summaries.
Maya: timeline good. Carlos 1 can you open a tiny RFC describing event change, ingest migration, and how older events are labeled unknown? include example event diff.
Carlos: will do. quick snippet for event change: ```json
{
  "chosen_model": "redwood/v1-small",
  "routing_reason": "priority",
  "lane_name": "fast-ssd",
  "lane_id": "lane_1234",
  "tenant_id": "acct_5678"
}
```
Mei: and add migration note: ingestion treats missing lane_id as null and routes those events into "unknown" bucket; materializer emits metric row with lane_id = "unknown".
Leo: final ask: color and ordering rules. lane color should be deterministic by lane_id hash and consistent across console. ordering: sort by tokens desc.
Maya: agreed. small polish: when user hovers a lane show top model variants and a tiny sample of recent p95 spikes (if any) with links to traces.
Carlos: I'll include API example response in RFC. keep it compact.
Maya: awesome. thanks everyone. will draft the UX mock + RFC and tag infra + telemetry.
infra-bot: note: feature flag exp/console-lane-summaries created. opt-in for orgs: test-inc, redwood-staging.
Mei: thanks. Ill add the privacy/obfuscation options to RFC before WeShip.
